🇲🇽 Mexico City has experienced significant cultural, economic, and social shifts following an influx of foreign tourists and expatriates, predominantly from the United States, resulting in considerable local apprehension. These developments have precipitated rising rental costs, gentrification, and perceived disrespect from certain visitors, prompting discourse surrounding “gringo racism”. The city’s appeal to foreign residents escalated substantially during the pandemic as remote working arrangements became prevalent. Long-term Airbnb bookings increased by more than 30% in 2022 relative to 2019, with short-term rentals now accounting for up to a quarter of housing in fashionable districts. Consequently, rents have nearly doubled, and certain job advertisements now stipulate English proficiency. Protests regarding gentrification and the elevated cost of living—where the average monthly salary remains below $400—are frequent, and anti-foreigner graffiti has emerged in districts such as Condesa and Roma.

According to the Financial Times, RAF Lakenheath, the largest U.S. fighter base in Europe, went on "Charlie alert" on November 13 after a swarm of 6 drones flew over the base. Charlie is the 2nd highest alert level. The USAF repelled the drones but did not recover them.
